_doc: THE STRIP BAN'S LIMIT, SAID AND TRACKED (REVIEW-W2B's third read, finding 2; the chair's ruling: before the release the ban is NOT rebuilt as a data-flow read). The reader's fifteen unwrap shapes (docs/chair/2026-11-13/probes/REVIEW-W2B-3/stripshapes.mjs on lane/review-w2b-2026-11-13 at cc0dd4ed2), copied verbatim, each with TODAY'S TRUTH through tests/lint/presumedThings.shared.mjs :: stripSites: 'caught' (the strip site and its receiver) or 'known-gap' (no site: the ban does not see this shape). The ban catches the shapes it names and no others. A seat that widens the ban moves a named row here from 'known-gap' to 'caught' in the same commit; the walker's test (presumedThings.walker.test.js, 'the strip ban's known gaps') asserts every row exactly. Measured at c3913f999: 3 caught, 12 known gaps (agrees with the reader).

const out = []; let i = 0; while (i < POOL.length) { out.push(POOL[i].text); i += 1; } export default out;
let out = []; for (const l of POOL) out = out.concat(l.text); export default out;
const out = []; for (const l of POOL) out[out.length] = l.text; export default out;
const { text } = pick(POOL); export default text;
const prop = (k) => (o) => o[k]; export const a = POOL.map(prop('text'));
const out = []; POOL.forEach((l) => Object.assign(out, { [out.length]: l.text })); export default out;
export const a = new Set(POOL.map((l) => l)).forEach ? [...POOL].map((l) => `${l.text}`) : [];
